items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public service law, in relation to requiring utility corporations to provide an annual transparency statement to customers
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6335

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the public service law, in relation
to requiring utility corporations to provide an annual transparency
statement to customers

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

This bill would require every utility to provide each customer with an
annual transparency statement, which shall detail charges on a gross
basis included in each customer's delivery service portion of their
utility bill including various taxes as well as charges and costs
imposed by the public service commission that are embedded in the
customer bill.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section one of the bill provides that commencing on January 1, 2019,
every utility corporation on an annual basis shall provide each
customer with an annual transparency statement which shall detail
charges included in each customer's delivery service portion of their
utility bill, including property taxes, sales and compensating use
taxes, costs and expenses of the Department of Public Service, gross
receipts taxes, franchise and income taxes, MTA authority payroll
taxes and fees, charges and costs imposed by the Public Service
Commission which are embedded in the customer bill.

Section two of the bill sets forth the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Electric bills are increasingly complex with numerous components. The
electric industry in New York State is in transition as the Public
Service Commission (PSC) implements Reforming the Energy Vision. In
addition, the Clean Energy Standard has been adopted by the PSC.
These programs will result in mandates on the utilities, which will
translate into additional costs for electric customers. The charges on
the electric utility bill are simplistically listed for delivery
services and supply services There are multiple constituent costs
included in supply services, which are continuing to evolve under the
new regulatory regime.

The requirement for utilities to provide an annual transparence
statement will assist customers in eliminating confusion about their
bills. It will also eliminate the perception by many that the
complexity is designed to conceal the cost structure. An annual
transparency statement provides the consumer with an opportunity to
examine and understand what costs are on their bill. The delineation
of charges such as legacy transition, municipal underground, clean
energy deliver, systems benefit, zero emissions credit, state and
local taxes provides the consumer with a detailed view of what's
behind the delivery services charge and its percentage impact on their
electric bill.

This information will encourage customers to be more cognizant of the
PSC's role in the cost of electricity on their bill. Many consumers do
not appreciate the costs, which are included in the delivery services
portion of their bill. These various charges constitute significant
cost drivers in their utility bill. This legislation is intended to
increase awareness, which could result in increased public
participation and interest in the PSC proceedings by members of the
general public. The charges on each customer's bill denotes public
policy choices. This bill would illuminate those choices.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

This is a new bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately
